newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee recovers, ends at day's high.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee recovers, ends at day's high.

text.p: Nearby robusta coffee futures recovered from early losses to end at the day's highs, aided by strengthening switches, traders said.
"The strengthening of the switches are underpinning the market," said one.
London's reversal from its early downtrend followed a further rally in New York after the December contract triggered some speculative buying on the way up.
By the finish, London's benchmark November contract stood $9 higher at $1,512 a tonne after touching the day's low of $1,494.
Second-position January was $6 firmer at $1,450 a tonne. Overall volume on the exchange reached 4,446 lots.
Traders said activity was dominated by nearby spread trading, with Nov/Jan and Jan/March structures leading the activity.
The widening Nov/Jan spread was seen trading at $61-$62 while Jan/March widened to around $41-$42 from Tuesday's finish of $37.
Traders said interest was also focused on the options.
The main underlying factor supporting both the London and New York markets was weekend's news of a sharp draw in U.S. certified stocks.
But traders in London said a more decisive factor is news that there is no coffee pending certification at the U.S. exchange warehouses.
"There's no fresh coffee beans awaiting for certification and that is probably more important than the fact that there was a drawdown in stocks," said one.
Broker GNI said there would not be much coffee around in the market until the beginning of December when the Central American crop arrives.
"GNI...therefore recommend buying the Dec/March spread and also December outright," it said in a daily commentary.
